title: Borel subgroups over arbitrary fields
statement: Let $F$ be any field [def-weil-field], and $B,H$ group schemes over $F$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. A homomorphism $i:B\to H$ is a field-relative Borel inclusion if it is a closed subgroup inclusion [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], $B$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], and solvable in the finite closed subnormal-series sense of [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure], and it is maximal with these properties. Explicitly, for every smooth connected solvable closed subgroup $j:D\to H$ and every homomorphism $f:B\to D$ with $j\circ f=i$, the map $f$ is an isomorphism. No algebraic-closedness assumption is made on $F$.

source.place: Definition 17.6, p.353; Chapter 21 standing arbitrary field, p.424; maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup convention in lem-sfb-split-flag-rational-fixed-scheme.
